currentSprint.name: Vertical Slice 01 — Christian and The Dreamer
currentSprint.resumeNote: 30-scene real-controls journey passes end to end (25.3m); v26 hero and City v5 remain visual-bar fails, while City draw-call budgets are now green for both desktop and mobile headless profiles.

workstreams.name: Independent baseline audit
workstreams.largestGap: Fresh critic scored visual shipping readiness 2.8/10; authored hero and world-scale environment art are largest gap.

workstreams.name: Christian protagonist
workstreams.critic: fresh runtime critic — fail, 6.8/10, comparison v26
workstreams.largestGap: v26 materially improves v22 with a tapered waist, longer/slimmer arms and lower body, articulated fingers, smaller boots, and darker adult eye materials. Adult readability, limbs, torso, hands, and boots pass focused layers. The single remaining gap is burden contact/material realism: the oversized black load still reads as a mounted shell with weak shoulder/waist compression.

workstreams.name: The Dreamer environment
workstreams.largestGap: Dream guided travel now uses monotonic authored bends, every clearing is reachable, and the medium collision runtime is mounted. The remaining gap is visual: the shrine, vegetation, and water still need a stronger focal hierarchy and authored asset fidelity.

workstreams.name: City of Destruction environment
workstreams.critic: fresh runtime critic — fail, 5.1/10, v5 comparison; perf follow-up within budget
workstreams.largestGap: v5 adds restrained facade/road wear, target-safe planters, instanced market citizens, stronger banners/crest, and richer street life while preserving cue/interact flow. The harsh critic still sees flat-color low-poly architecture with weak material breakup, sparse skyline life, and insufficient authored atmosphere versus Kena/Pathless/RiME. Performance follow-up measures 7.08s desktop / 4.84s mobile headless ready, 150 desktop / 98 mobile draw calls p95, and 28,308 / 24,772 triangles p95; these are SwiftShader evidence, not hardware FPS.

workstreams.name: The Wicket Gate authored beat
workstreams.critic: fresh live critic — fail, visual bar; gameplay contract now passes
workstreams.largestGap: The six beats now share real gate anchors, animated leaves/bolts, Goodwill reveal, entry bounds, and telegraphed swept arrows; the desktop arrow-impact and full traversal suites are green. The remaining gap is authored rendering quality: low-poly masonry/vegetation, flat path, and weak material depth versus the keyframe bar.

workstreams.name: Delectable Mountains to Celestial City finale
workstreams.critic: focused real-controls finale smoke test — pass, 2.2m
workstreams.largestGap: Five new chapters complete Part One through the River and Celestial City with authored lighting, water, skyline, and watchfulness motifs. The remaining gap is a fresh visual critic pass and dedicated finale audio beds; River mobile tier is 96 draw calls p95 after its compact presentation.

workstreams.name: Mobile touch movement
workstreams.largestGap: Directional controls now capture the pointer and release on up, cancel, or lost capture; physical-device Safari gesture validation remains outstanding.

workstreams.name: Audio safety and browser unlock
workstreams.largestGap: Legacy scene and SFX calibration is clamped before the shared limiter, unlock requests are coalesced, transient voices are capped, and AudioContext interruptions now update the HUD and recover on gesture. Dedicated finale beds and physical-device listening QA remain outstanding.

workstreams.name: Performance and loading
workstreams.largestGap: Gate remains 5.60s desktop / 4.44s mobile at 3.8 / 6.6 headless FPS with 124 / 88 draw-call p95; the new River finale tier is 7.06s desktop / 6.97s mobile at 142 / 96 draw-call p95 and 41,142 / 39,038 triangles. Hardware FPS, cold-start variance, and authored visual fidelity remain release blockers.

workstreams.name: Live progress board
workstreams.largestGap: Lazyweb MCP tools are unavailable in this task; data feed is live, visual board awaits connector refresh.
